name: Castuera concentration camp (La Verilleja)
story: When the Republican Army of Extremadura surrendered at the end of March 1939, Nationalist authorities built a camp on the La Verilleja estate about 3 km from Castuera, in the La Serena district. For about a year it held thousands of Republican soldiers and civilians awaiting classification and trial; many were taken out and shot, some reportedly at nearby mine shafts. The camp was laid out with a perimeter ditch, streets of barracks, a central square with a cross, latrines and washrooms. In 2009 it was declared a Bien de Interés Cultural (historic site) — one of the best-preserved Francoist camp layouts in Spain.
see: On the ground: the perimeter ditch, main gate area, paved camp streets, barrack foundations and the cement base of the cross; memorial markers placed by the memory association.
plan: Site is within private farmland; access is along a marked track from the Castuera–Benquerencia road — ask at Castuera tourist office or the Asociación Memorial Campo de Concentración de Castuera about access and annual commemorative walks.

boxes.text: view it from the road or public path only.
Prisoner numbers range from 8,000–9,000 (Julián Chaves) to 15,000–20,000 in other estimates; the number executed is not established.
